top_cluster.headline: Emily Moreno, ex-wife of Rep. Max Miller (R-Ohio), has filed a federal lawsuit against him alleging a sensitive/nude photo of their young daughter was made public.
top_cluster.left_framing: The Washington Post frames this as an act of recklessness by a Republican congressman who endangered his own child while trying to defend himself against domestic abuse allegations — emphasizing the unsecured Dropbox mishandling and situating the incident within a larger pattern of alleged misconduct by Miller.
top_cluster.center_framing: The Hill presents the story primarily as a serious legal matter, centering the lawsuit's allegations in neutral, fact-forward language without connecting it to broader political context or editorializing on Miller's culpability.
top_cluster.right_framing: No right-leaning source was included in the provided coverage, so right-of-center framing cannot be characterized from this set.
top_cluster.left_omissions: The Washington Post's framing does not present the more direct, unqualified allegation language used by The Hill (that Miller 'posted' the photo), instead foregrounding the Dropbox/document-release mechanism, which somewhat softens the directness of the accusation while amplifying the negligence and domestic-abuse angle.
top_cluster.right_omissions: No right-leaning source is available in this set to compare; it's unknown whether right-leaning outlets have covered this story at all or how they would frame it.

blindspot_narrative: The right is systematically avoiding stories where its own actors look bad (Miller lawsuit, ICE misconduct) while amplifying Democratic Party dysfunction narratives and institutional-fraud framing against left-coded organizations (SPLC). The left is avoiding sustained self-examination of its primary results and largely ignoring the SPLC prosecution's substance, instead focusing on process/motivation questions. Both patterns suggest each side is optimizing today's coverage for pre-existing midterm narratives rather than following the news value of individual stories.
